title: How TED Talks Work: Featuring Roman Mars
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss TED Talks: the origin of TED (Richard Saul Wurman's 1984 first conference, the Sony compact disc and Macintosh demos, Benoit Mandelbrot's fractal talk), Chris Anderson buying TED and making it a nonprofit, the 18-minute format and online release in 2006, how speakers are coached and must memorize scripts, tips for public speaking, criticisms of TED as elitist and "lying" about changing the world, and TED's ticket and prize economics. The episode includes an interview with Roman Mars of 99% Invisible and Radiotopia about his TED talk on city flag design, in which he describes the preparation, the audience, and the reception of his talk. The episode closes with a listener mail about a family scattering cremated remains and a sign-off.

segments.title: Live show announcements and Squarespace sponsor read
segments.summary: Sponsor read for Squarespace, then announcements of spring live shows in Seattle, Portland, Houston, and Denver with ticket info.

segments.title: Opening banter and International Women's Day clarification
segments.summary: Hosts clarify that a previous makeup episode was not meant to offend, and banter about whiskey samples, hangovers, and band names.

segments.title: What TED stands for and its cultural role
segments.summary: Josh explains TED stands for technology, entertainment, and design, not a person's name. They discuss how TED fits into Silicon Valley technocratic idealism, the 18-minute attention span claim, and why the format suits social media, with TED releasing talks online for free starting in 2006.

segments.title: Origins of TED: Richard Saul Wurman's first conference
segments.summary: The first TED conference in 1984 was organized by designer Richard Saul Wurman as an anti-conference, a dinner-party style gathering. Featured demos included the Sony compact disc player and the Macintosh computer, and mathematician Benoit Mandelbrot spoke. The early event lost money, and Wurman later sold TED to Chris Anderson, who ran it as a nonprofit and introduced the 18-minute format and online release.

segments.title: TED locations, TEDx versus TED, and speaker preparation
segments.summary: TED moved from Monterey to Long Beach in 2009 and to Vancouver in 2014. The hosts distinguish TED from local TEDx events. They describe how speakers spend six to nine months crafting a script with TED staff, must memorize talks word for word, and are coached intensively, with Tim Urban's Wait But Why account as an example.

segments.title: Public speaking tips and TED stage conventions
segments.summary: The hosts discuss TED guidelines: no teleprompters or note cards, eye contact with friendly faces in the audience, limited movement, and personal journey framing. They discuss Susan Cain's popular TED talk on introverts and note that Bill Gates named it a favorite.

segments.title: Criticisms of TED: elitism, idealism, and cost
segments.summary: The hosts review critiques of TED, including Frank Rich's Harper's essay Ted Talks Are Lying to You, Benjamin Bratton's takedown, and claims that TED talks spread ideas without changing the world. They discuss attendee costs (ticket prices, membership fees, application requirements), the unpaid speakers, and TED Prize winners such as Bono, Bill Clinton, and Jamie Oliver. They also reflect on how critiques should be constructive.

segments.title: Transition to interview with Roman Mars
segments.summary: The hosts tease the upcoming interview with Roman Mars of 99% Invisible and Radiotopia, who gave a real TED talk.

segments.title: Interview with Roman Mars about his TED talk on flag design
segments.summary: Roman Mars describes his TED talk on city flag design, how he chose the topic, the nerves of the process, his decision to present in a radio-style format at a table with sound and visuals, and the supportive audience. He reflects on TED's social culture, his skepticism about solutionism, and the impact on his podcasts.

segments.title: Wrap-up of TED episode and recommended reading
segments.summary: Hosts close the TED discussion, suggesting listeners search TED Talks and read the HowStuffWorks article on the topic, then transition to listener mail.

segments.title: Listener mail: scattered cremated remains
segments.summary: Emily writes that her late father's cremated remains were placed in small bottles for guests, and scattered in places including the Vango Museum in Amsterdam, the Bellagio fountain in Las Vegas, and Iceland. The hosts respond to the story from the earlier cremation episode.

segments.title: Sign-off and contact information
segments.summary: Hosts give social media and email contact information and the website.
